slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A convex n-gon can be split from one vertex into n − 2 triangles.

Interior angle sum = (n − 2) times 180 degrees. Exterior angle sum (one at each vertex) = 360 degrees, for every convex polygon.

Walking around a convex polygon, you turn at each corner by its exterior angle and end facing the way you started, one full turn of 360 degrees. Algebra agrees: each exterior plus interior angle is 180, so the exterior sum is 180n − (n − 2)180 = 360.
